text: Professional Overview: The Computer Science and Technology major focuses on the structure and operation of computer software and hardware, the development and programming of computer systems, as well as the theoretical and practical methods of various information processing engineering. The aim is to cultivate students' mastery of the basic knowledge of mathematics and natural sciences, as well as the fundamental theories, knowledge, skills and methods related to computing systems, and to equip them with scientific thinking abilities such as computational thinking, as well as the ability to design computing solutions and implement systems based on computing principles, so as to provide high-quality specialized technical talents for related fields such as computing system research, development, deployment and application.Curriculum systemGeneral education courses: These include courses in the humanities and social sciences (such as career planning, ideological and moral cultivation, and legal basis, etc.), mathematics (such as calculus, probability theory, and mathematical statistics, etc.), and natural sciences (such as college physics), accounting for approximately 15% of the total courses.Disciplinary basic courses: including knowledge points such as programming, data structures, computer organization, operating systems, computer networks, and information management, they are an important foundation for professional learning.Professional courses: There are fields such as digital circuits, computer system architecture, algorithms, programming languages, software engineering, parallel and distributed computing, intelligent technology, computer graphics and human-computer interaction, accounting for about 30% of the total courses.Practical teaching: It accounts for approximately 20% of the total courses, including experimental courses, course design, internships, and graduation projects, etc. It requires that the total experimental equivalent over four years be no less than 20,000 lines of code to cultivate students' practical abilities and the capacity to solve real-world problems.
